Senses.PreferredTarget: the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West
AlternateTargets: what the Patriarch came from the West for
the point of Bodhidharma's coming from the West
Senses.Explanation: A fixed liturgical question, almost always in the frame (如何是祖師西來意) — 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West?' The Patriarch is Bodhidharma (the First Patriarch); 'coming from the West' is his journey from India to China, so the question literally asks why he came and what he brought. In the records it is one of the most common test-questions a monk puts to a master, and the recorded answers are turning-words rather than explanations — Zhaozhou 'the cypress tree in the front garden' (庭前柏樹子), Xianglin 'you sit long and get tired' (坐久成勞), Longya 'when the stone tortoise talks I'll tell you', Guishan 'what a fine lantern' (大好燈籠), Mazu answers with a kick to the chest. Linji's record engages the question on its own word (意): (問)。(如何是西來意)。(師云)。(若有意)。(自救不了)。(云)。(既無意)。(云何二祖得法)。(師云)。(得者是不得) ('If there were a meaning, he could not save even himself.' — 'If there is no meaning, how did the Second Patriarch obtain the teaching?' — 'The getting is not-getting'); the same record has Zhaozhou put the question while Linji is washing his feet and receive (恰值老僧洗脚) ('you happen to catch this old monk washing his feet'), and Longya — handed the Chan board (禪板) he was told to fetch and struck with it — reply (打即任打)。(要且無祖師意) ('hit me if you like; still there is no Patriarch's meaning'), the whole exchange then repeating at Cuiwei with a cushion. Xiangyan's tree case states the stakes of the question itself: (樹下有人)。(問西來意)。(不對即違他所問)。(若對又喪身失命) ('someone under the tree asks the meaning of the coming from the West; not answering fails his question, answering costs body and life'). The records also pair it with the scriptural teaching: the double-question (祖意教意是同是別) ('are the Patriarch's meaning and the teaching's meaning the same or different?') is itself a stock question, and Zhaozhou's own record answers it (會得祖意)。(便會教意) ('understand the Patriarch's meaning and you understand the teaching's meaning'). Render it literally — 'the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West'.
Senses.Note: Overwhelmingly attested: 1736 raw occurrences across 239 allowlist texts. The five curated occurrences are chosen as classic, mutually independent answers to the stock question. Frame counts (462-text allowlist grep): the fixed question (如何是祖師西來意) 1858 hits in 231 texts; short forms (西來意) 3071 in 314 and (祖師意) 645 in 185; intensified (西來的的意) 112 in 54; (達磨西來) 494 in 181; the answer-tag (庭前柏樹子) 317 in 130; the paired question (祖意教意是同是別) 32 in 19. Refs: Linji material T47n1985 0502a08 (若有意。自救不了), 0504a16 (恰值老僧洗脚), 0504b03–06 (龍牙/翠微); Xiangyan tree case T48n2005 0293c03; Zhaozhou's (會得祖意)。(便會教意) J24nB137 0367b30.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問趙州：『如何是祖師西來意？』州云：『庭前柏樹子。』僧云：『和尚莫將境示人。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The most famous answer: Zhaozhou answers with 'the cypress tree in the front garden.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 不見水潦和尚問馬大師云：如何是祖師西來意？馬大師欄胸一踏倒，水潦從地起來，忽然大省
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Mazu answers Shuiliao's question with a kick to the chest — the wordless reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 香林遠禪師。僧問：「如何是祖師西來意？」遠云：「坐久成勞。」
僧問龍牙：『如何是祖師西來意？』牙云：『待石烏龜解語即向汝道。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 'Wait till the stone tortoise can talk (待石烏龜解語即向汝道).'

Occurrences.Kwic: 仰山問溈山云：「如何是祖師西來意？」溈云：「大好燈籠。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Guishan answers Yangshan with 'what a fine lantern.'
